children: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) extended their rally on Friday as investors bought super-long maturities to unwind curve-steepening trades on expectations the Bank of Japan will accelerate rate hikes.
The 30-year yield (JP30YTN=JBTC) fell 10.5 basis points (bps) to 3.97%. The 40-year bond yield (JP40YTN=JBTC) fell 13 bps to 4.03%. Yields move inversely to bond prices.

"Investors had been betting on a curve steepening as they were worried about the BOJ falling behind the curve in dealing with inflation," said Masayuki Koguchi, executive chief fund manager at Mitsubishi UFJ Asset Management.
"But with the BOJ's rate-hike bets growing and the yen strengthening, they are closing those positions and betting on curve flattening," he said.
Declines in shorter-dated bond yields were more muted, with the policy-sensitive two-year yield (JP2YTN=JBTC) down 2 basis points at 1.83%.

Swap rates indicate a 97% chance for the BOJ to raise its policy rate by 25 bps to 1.25% at its September meeting, according to money market broker Tokyo Tanshi. Traders also fully priced in another rate hike to 1.5% by the January meeting.
The sharp rally at the super-long end was also fuelled by bets that a stronger yen would ease inflationary pressure by lowering import costs.

The yen has gained in recent sessions partly on speculation that Japan's Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) could increase allocations to domestic bonds and other yen-denominated assets following recent meetings.

Recent calls by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent for Japan to end its reflationary policies also helped reverse trends in the yen and Japanese government bonds, said Katsutoshi Inadome, senior strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.

"Bessent's remarks may not be powerful enough to stop the selloff of JGBs in the long term, as his comments could affect Japan's monetary policy, but Japan's fiscal policy may not change," Inadome said.
